part_dispositions.text: S2 reports a replication of the self-reported feelings-of-power effect
reasons: The paper explicitly says it replicated the feelings-of-power finding (two-tailed, p = .017, d = 0.344). Caveats: modest effect, 5 missing, conceptual replication.

part_dispositions.text: S2 reports no hormonal effect of power posing
reasons: Testosterone (p = .162) and cortisol (p = .272) not significant two-tailed; title 'No Effect on Hormones'; Discussion 'failed to confirm'.

part_dispositions.text: S2 reports no behavioral effect of power posing
reasons: No significant effect in any of the three behavioral tasks; statistics given only for gain-domain risk; Discussion says power 'did not yield behavioral effects'.
The proposition closely paraphrases the paper's own summary sentence and Discussion; all three parts are reported as stated.

Qualifications concern precision, not direction; chiefly that 'no effect' means 'no statistically significant effect'. A stricter reader could grade the whole SUPPORTS_WITH_QUALIFICATION on that point alone (reviewer's words).

locator_note: The reviewer quoted with normalized punctuation and elisions; each cited passage was mapped by the primary session to its exact span in the pinned extraction. The reviewer's own wording is in the response file.

qualifications.point: Non-significance, not proven absence; >95% power only for Carney et al.'s effect size (details in supplement).
Point estimates run opposite to Carney et al. (gain-domain risk d = -0.176, testosterone d = -0.200, cortisol d = -0.157); strengthens rather than weakens the null reading.
Uneven reporting across behavioral tasks: statistics only for gain-domain risk.
Robustness claims deferred to the supplement.
Conceptual replication; protocol differences; authors allow omitted conditions may explain nulls.
Sequential sampling: design caveat, not a contradiction.

contrary_search.found: None in the main text; subgroups summarized as 'similar'.

contrary_search.searched_for: Passages claiming a hormonal or behavioral effect

strongest_contrary_interpretation: 'Replication' is fair (the paper's own word), but critics could note a conceptual replication with a weak effect and end-of-session self-report; 'no effects' overstates findings that are only non-significant, two of three behavioral tasks lack statistics, and the authors allow protocol differences may have removed needed conditions. These concern precision and generalization, not misstatement.
what_would_change: Supplemental Material showing a significant hormonal or behavioral effect in a subsample or specification summarized as 'similar' (relevant part to SUPPORTS_WITH_QUALIFICATION).
An audit standard distinguishing 'no effect' from 'no significant effect' (parts b, c and overall to SUPPORTS_WITH_QUALIFICATION).
